title: Introduce RAG storyboard templates and live-snippet runner
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a lightweight storyboard-based RAG quickstart and an interactive snippet runner for fast authoring and telemetered dev iteration.
description: Motivation: internal and external developer feedback requested a compact, story-driven RAG quickstart focused on authoring small narrative scenarios (storyboards) that combine few-shot prompts, tool calls, and structured output assertions. Goal: provide a set of storyboard templates, an opinionated file layout for stepwise scenarios, and a tiny live-runner that executes individual steps against a local dev index or hosted Redwood API for fast iteration. Summary of changes: added a new examples/rag/storyboard quickstart with multiple templates (faq-style, walkthrough, multi-tool flow), a runner utility (Python) with optional Docker and shell wrappers, CI smoke job for the quickstart, docsite page and snippet gallery, and unit tests for runner logic. Checklist: - [x] add templates and examples - [x] add runner + shell wrapper - [x] add docs/snippets for docsite - [x] add CI smoke job - [x] add unit tests - [x] telemetry hooks for dev-only traces Important notes: the runner is intended for developer iteration only and defaults to sandbox credentials; production deployment guidance is documented in docs/snippets/storyboard.md. Security: removed hardcoded keys, added env-file example and KMS note. How to try: 1) git clone the repo; 2) cd examples/rag/storyboard; 3) cp .env.example .env and set REDWOOD_API_KEY or run with --local-index; 4) ./run-storyboard.sh templates/walkthrough.yaml to step through each storyboard step in the terminal. Related: follows ENG-1824 (storyboard UX) and DOC-403 (docsite gallery).
